verdict.rationale: Solo 2's GitHub README says the device speaks passkeys/WebAuthn (FIDO2), PIV and OpenPGP, the three mechanisms the story names, and the product docs say a touch on the capacitive sensor confirms operations. Nothing in the pack explicitly documents SSH use: no sk-ssh key generation, no PIV or OpenPGP SSH setup, and no touch-policy configuration for SSH. An older HN comment saying it 'doesn't do OpenPGP' predates the current README and is not a concrete hands-on failure. Missing for 10: explicit SSH documentation (ed25519-sk/ecdsa-sk with OpenSSH, PIV or OpenPGP SSH workflows), documented touch-required policy for SSH signing, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, my SSH keys can be hardware-backed on the device — via FIDO2 sk-ssh keys, PIV, or OpenPGP — so server access requires a physical touch

citations.quote: It's a USB+NFC device that protects your accounts with passkeys/WebAuthn, and also speaks OATH (TOTP/HOTP), PIV, and OpenPGP.
When prompted, touch the capacitive sensor on your Solo 2 to confirm.
